thread:
sam: Heads-up — I'm planning to land a Terraform change to add autoscaling for NAT instances and wire PrivateLink interface endpoints' security groups. Target canary apply next Tue 02:00 PT. Quick questions: (1) Do PrivateLink interface endpoints need explicit route table assoc for our setup? (2) Any gotchas for NAT autoscale + EIP allocation we should call out for oncall? @ops-bot tagging for apply window and handoff.

ops-bot: FYI — default infra apply window available Tue 02:00-03:00 PT. Pager oncall: jordan. Reminder: include rollback steps in PR body.

kai: you don't need route table assoc if the endpoint is an interface endpoint in a subnet that has normal routing — traffic flows through the ENIs. BUT you do need to ensure the endpoint's SG allows inbound from our service ENIs / pods. Share the TF snippet?

sam: here's roughly what I'm adding for the endpoint — open to feedback:

```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "metrics_api" {
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.us-west-2.execute-api"
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids   = var.appliance_subnets
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.plumb.id]
}
```

sam: and the NAT autoscaling module (simplified):

```
module "nat_asg" {
  source         = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infrastructure-modules.git//nat-asg"
  desired_capacity = 2
  max_size         = 8
  eip_pool_tag     = "shared-nat-eips"
}
```

elena: couple notes from networking/security ops: (a) watch SNAT port exhaustion — autoscaling helps but if connections churn you can hit ephemeral port limits. Increase `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` on clients where possible and make EIP pool ample. (b) tag EIPs and add IAM guardrails so autoscaler picks from correct pool. (c) before scaling down, prefer draining NAT instances rather than immediate terminate to avoid mid-connection drops.

kai: also watch route/propagation order if we have a TGW attachment in the VPC. During canary if TGW routes are learned they might override local route table changes. Recommend explicit `aws_route` entries with the desired `route_table_id` pointing 0.0.0.0/0 -> natgw id, and use a short canary window.

jordan: I'll be oncall for the window. sam — please add me as reviewer on the PR and put a clear rollback section. If we need to roll back, we want: (1) scale ASG back to desired_capacity=2, (2) detach EIPs gracefully, (3) reassign any replaced resolver rules. Tag PR with `infra:rollback` section.

sam: will do. One final DNS question — if we change resolver rules to forward privatelink domains to shared-resolver, will that break hostnames used by pods during canary? I want to avoid a half-up DNS state.

elena: safe pattern is conditional TF variable `canary = true` that creates resolver changes only in the canary account. Keep the production resolver untouched until the canary validates. Also include TTL/short-cache DNS test.

kai: small verification step for canary: spin a small test pod and curl the endpoint by DNS name from inside the cluster (non-hostNetwork). Example: `kubectl run --rm -it --image=amazonlinux nettest -- bash` then `curl https://{api-private-host}/health`. If DNS fails or times out, abort.

sam: adding those into the PR checklist: 1) E2E pod curl test, 2) EIP pool tagging present, 3) ASG scaling policy sane, 4) rollback steps, 5) ops oncall ack.

ops-bot: Apply job scheduled: infra/plan/2465123456 -> apply window Tue 02:00-03:00 PT. Use `infra apply --canary` for the dry run first.

jordan: noted. I'll monitor and can drop a rollback if we see port exhaustion or DNS regressions. :thumbsup:

elena: one extra nit — set lifecycle ignore_changes for `aws_vpc_endpoint`'s `private_dns_enabled` if we expect providers to toggle it during test, so TF doesn't flip it back automatically.

sam: good catch. Thanks everyone — I'll open the PR shortly and ping this thread when plan is green.

kai: LGTM, small docs reminder: update infra runbook with ASG drain script and EIP reclaim playbook.
